title: RBAC v2 atomic switchover checklist and telemetry gating
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Execute an atomic switchover from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 for the main control plane with minimal customer disruption and strong audit fidelity. This ticket produces a prescriptive checklist, telemetry gate definitions, and operational playbook for the switchover window. Scope includes: pre-cutover validation suite, dual-write shadowing sanity checks, backfill verification, SSO/SAML mapping validation, admin-role rollback hooks, audit-log continuity, and customer communications templates. Out of scope: long-tail historical role cleanup post-cutover (handled by ENG-314159).
success_criteria: 1) No customer 5xx auth failures attributable to role mapping during canary + main cutover; 2) Audit logs show continuous event sequences for role grants/revocations (no gaps) for the cutover interval; 3) Telemetry gating prevents main cutover if any gate trips; 4) Two documented and tested rollback paths that restore service within the SLA; 5) Customer comms templates ready and reviewed by legal and support.
cutover_plan_summary: Day -7: Run full dry-run in staging with synthetic traffic, exercise backfill tooling, and run SSO mapping verification. Day -3: Narrow canary cohort (internal teams + opt-in customers). Day -1: Freeze non-critical deploys. T-0: Enable RBAC v2 read-through with dual-write to v1 and v2. T+30m: Evaluate telemetry gates. If green, flip authoritative flag to RBAC v2. T+24h: Progressive expansion to all tenants with increased monitoring. Post +48h: Run reconciliation backfill and close the change window.
telemetry_gates: Auth 5xx rate < 0.05% across canary tenants (15 min window)
Top 10 affected routes latency delta < 20ms median vs baseline
Audit log ingestion lag < 30s for all regions
Role mapping mismatch rate < 0.02% (lookup failures / total lookups)
SSO assertion failures < 0.01% for canary orgs
pre_migration_checks: Export role snapshots for a stratified sample of 200 orgs
Run idempotent backfill in shadow mode and compare checksums
Validate SAML attribute mappings against 15 federated customers' config
Run chaos tests that kill primary auth nodes and validate automatic fallback
Confirm KMS/HSM access for audit log signing service
backfill_strategy: Dual-write shadowing for 72 hours with continuous reconciliation runs. Backfill jobs run in prioritized waves by org size and security sensitivity. Each backfill job produces a delta report: additions, removals, conflicts, and human-review flags. Conflicts are routed to a triage queue for manual review by Security Ops.
rollback_paths: Soft rollback: flip authoritative flag back to RBAC v1 within control plane (expected ~5 mins to take effect); keep v2 as passive for diagnosis
Hard rollback: disable v2 endpoints and restore v1-only writes, initiate on-call runbook and customer notice (expected ~30-45 mins if coord with infra)
audit_and_compliance: Ensure continuous audit event sequence by using our event-UUID passthrough. Audit pipeline will be validated with a checksum comparison pre and post cutover. Retention and immutable storage settings will be preserved; a signed snapshot will be taken at T-15m to have an authoritative point-in-time export for compliance teams.
sso_saml_notes: During dual-write shadow, enrich mappings with a 'mapping_source' metadata tag so mismatches can be attributed to v1/v2 differences. Run test SAML assertions (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated) for the list of federated customers included in the canary. Add automated remediation suggestions for common attribute mapping issues.
customer_communications: We will send an initial 7-day notice to customers in the canary cohort and an expanded 72-hour notice to all customers before the main cutover. Communications include expected timelines, possible transient auth errors, how to opt-out of early waves, and support contact escalation paths. Template versions: internal-beta, public-notice, partner-ops.

notes: This ticket emphasizes an atomic authoritative flip with conservative telemetry gating rather than a prolonged shadow-only migration. The intent is to minimize time windows where customers might observe divergence between control-plane reads and writes. Post-cutover, we'll spin out ENG follow-ups for long-term cleanup and analytics validation.
